newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank to open rediscount window.
newsitem.headline: China central bank to open rediscount window.

text.p: China's central bank, the People's Bank of China, plans to open a rediscount window to the four big state banks, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The newspaper gave no other details, saying only that this was part of plans to place more emphasis on monetary policy in 1997.
The previous practice of controlling money supply through mandatory directions on the credit scale of domestic banks had failed, the newspaper said, quoting central bank officials.
In the next two years, the bank would transform the system into one of self-control under central bank supervision, they said.
The central bank had set a ceiling for currency issue this year of 120 billion yuan ($14.5 billion), up by 13.6 percent compared with 1996, they said.

In addition to a decision to reduce bank reserve ratios -- expected to be cut to 9 percent from 13 percent -- the bank would expand trading on the interbank market to ensure it becomes the main vehicle for banks to balance their positions, the newspaper quoted bank officials as saying.
The officials gave no details of changes planned for the interbank market.
The bank plans to allow interest rates to play a bigger role in control of money supply, they said.
State media has said the central bank is expected to increase its quota for bank loans for 1997 to more than 800 billion yuan.
China's four big state banks, the main banks covered by the quota system, extended a total of 793.7 billion yuan in loans in 1996, up from 638.7 billion yuan in 1995, state media has said.

The central bank, the People's Bank of China, has considered phasing out the quotas for credit and loans, a remnant of central planning and has begun allowing some banks to lend purely on the basis of their reserves and debt-to-equity ratio.
